title: Update MIME type list to use IANA-registered names
body:
As of an hour before opening this PR, Godot's MIME types / media types are officially registered with IANA. This PR updates Godot's own files to use them. The new types are:

- `application/vnd.godot.project.binary`
- `application/vnd.godot.project.text`
- `application/vnd.godot.resource.binary`
- `application/vnd.godot.resource.text`
- `model/vnd.godot.scene.binary`
- `model/vnd.godot.scene.text`
- `text/vnd.godot.gdscript`
- `text/vnd.godot.gdshader`

These use the `vnd.godot` prefix reserved by IANA for the Godot Foundation, which replaces the `x-` application-specific prefix found in the old set of MIME types, which this PR is replacing:

- `application/x-godot-project`
- `application/x-godot-resource`
- `application/x-godot-scene`
- `application/x-godot-shader`
- `application/x-gdscript`

Additionally, the new MIME types have these structural differences:

- The `.binary` and `.text` versions of project, resource, and scene are split. This is due to IANA's requirements, I initially proposed to IANA to have just `application/vnd.godot.resource` etc, but they said different encodings need to have different MIME types.
- The scene formats are placed under `model/`, better categorizing them with other similar file types like glTF.
- The GDScript and GDShader formats are placed under `text/`, giving a better hint to text editors or text viewers that they can open the files, assuming such software makes judgements based on MIME type.

The `<icon name="x-godot-project"/>` etc entries in the Linux XML file were left alone, so that icon themes keep working. If changing these is also desired, let me know and I can amend this PR.

## Additional information

AI usage disclaimer: Most of the macOS plist file changes are AI-generated, because I am not familiar with plist files.

The AI flagged an existing problem with `UTTypeIdentifier`, where Godot was using names like `public.tscn`. Apple states that applications should use domain-qualified names rather than `public.*` ones. Changes to these are included. The AI also confirmed that new `UTTypeIdentifier` entries are required to handle the split binary/text types.

Aside from these two aspects, the changes are very straightforward/mechanical/menial, I'm confident that I could produce near-byte-identical results by hand with these two facts in mind. Also, the plist files pass `plutil -lint`. Still, the macOS plist files should be reviewed by a macOS plist expert such as @bruvzg.
